classification.difficultyReason: Find an intersection using the addition rule, then subtract it from B; recognise that mutually exclusive events have no intersection.

content.prompt:
Two events, $A$ and $B$, are such that $P(A)=\frac35$ and $P(B)=\frac14$.

If $A'$ denotes the complement of $A$, calculate $P(A'\cap B)$ when:

answer.worked:
Using the addition rule:
$$\begin{align*}P(A\cup B)&=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)\\\frac34&=\frac35+\frac14-P(A\cap B)\\P(A\cap B)&=\frac35+\frac14-\frac34\\P(A\cap B)&=\frac1{10}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(A'\cap B)&=P(B)-P(A\cap B)\\P(A'\cap B)&=\frac14-\frac1{10}\\P(A'\cap B)&=\frac3{20}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
Since $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, $P(A\cap B)=0$.
$$\begin{align*}P(A'\cap B)&=P(B)-P(A\cap B)\\P(A'\cap B)&=\frac14-0\\P(A'\cap B)&=\frac14\end{align*}$$
